narrative: Material PL1__M98C617E exhibits smooth, high-volume demand averaging 127,122 units per working day with a CV of 0.49, indicating moderate variability. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.69, range 0.05–4.84 days), making lead-time variance the dominant risk driver at 77.9% of total sigma_LTD. The recommended (r,Q) policy addresses the zero-safety-stock gap in SAP by introducing a 290,933-unit buffer, sized to achieve the 95% service level target. Order quantities are set at 436,651 units (EOQ-driven, MOQ-compliant, capacity-checked), reducing annual ordering events from 1,304 to 73 and delivering an estimated 81.5% reduction in total annual inventory costs.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous Review Policy with Combined Variability Safety Stock
research_insights.selection_rationale: Given smooth, high-volume daily demand and unstable lead times, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is appropriate. It triggers a fixed replenishment order of Q units whenever inventory falls to the reorder point r, combining demand and lead-time variance in the safety stock formula (sigma_LTD). This avoids over-ordering while ensuring buffer adequacy under lead-time spikes.
